entries.title: Bears match Seahawks' physicality, lead at halftime
entries.summary: <p>SEATTLE — In their first game since they declared their postseason dreams to the rest of the league, the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> did something to the Seahawks that no one had done in 27 games: they scored on the first drive.</p><p>And what a drive it was: 17 plays for 80 grueling yards over a whopping eight minutes and 32 seconds. Receiver Luther Burden’s fourth catch of the drive was his shortest — a 1-yard touchdown.</p><p>With that, the Bears proved that they could do one of the toughest things in the sport — match the physicality of the defending Super Bowl champions. When the Bears ran into the locker room with a 13-9 lead, it was clear that the Bears were who they believe themselves to be: contenders for the NFC title.</p><p>Quarterback Caleb Williams hung in the pocket and delivered throw after throw with a hand in his face, finishing the half 17-for-25 for 165 yards and a 99.6 passer rating. The Bears had 208 yards in the first half against a Seahawks defense that, thus far this season, had allowed 234 per game.</p><p>Defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, for whom the Bears sent the Titans two first round picks and a fourth-rounder last week, made his presence known early, sacking Sam Darnold in the first quarter. His new teammates matched his intensity, allowing only three first downs on the Seahawks’ five possessions before their touchdown-scoring drive. He led the Bears with five tackles in the first half, a rare feat for a defensive tackle.</p><p>The two sides traded second-quarter field goals, a 27-yard Jason Myers kick into the north end zone and a 44-yard Cairo Santos boot into the north end.</p><p>The Bears took over at the Seahawks 28 with about five minutes to play and marched downfield with relative ease. Rome Odunze caught an 18-yard pass, his first of the game. Two plays later, the Bears snapped the ball to running back D’Andre Swift, who handed off to Williams, who was lined up in the left slot, on a reverse. Williams pulled up and threw to Odunze, who was lined up left and ran a post route, for 24 yards.</p><p>Left with fourth-and-two from the Seahawks’ 20 with 1:12 left in the first half, the Bears lined up and let Williams try to draw Seattle offside on a hard count. When the Seahawks wouldn’t jump, Ben Johnson called a timeout and Santos came out to make a 38-yard field goal.</p><p>The Seahawks took possession and scored their first touchdown of the game with 30 seconds left after superstar Jaxon Smith-Njigba beat Tyrique Stevenson on a deep ball down the left sideline for a 43-yard touchdown. Smith-Njigba, who entered the weekend as the NFL’s receiving yards leader, had four catches for 92 yards in the first half.</p><p>Myers then missed the extra point.</p>
entries.author: Patrick Finley

entries.title: Bears notebook: QB Caleb Williams wears logo-less Caddix cleats vs. Seahawks to avoid more trouble with NFL
entries.summary: <p>SEATTLE — <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> quarterback <b>Caleb Williams</b> relented in his confrontation with the NFL over his cleats by wearing an all-black, logo-less pair Monday against the Seahawks.</p><p>The league <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/25/bears-qb-caleb-williams-fined-11-941-for-wearing-tom-brady-backed-caddix-cleats-another-fine-likely-coming" >fined Williams a total of $35,823 for wearing Caddix cleats</a> with a noticeable logo in recent games against the Falcons and Patriots because it violated its partnership with Nike, Under Armour and adidas. Players are not allowed to promote any non-partner brands on game days.</p><p>Rather than digging in harder, perhaps following former Bears quarterback <b>Jim McMahon</b>’s famous move of writing commissioner <b>Pete Rozelle</b>’s name on his headband after Rozelle fined him for an unauthorized adidas headband, Williams sought to make peace before it turned into an issue in which the league could prevent him from taking the field.</p><p>The NFL’s rulebook has a section that says officials can bar a player from playing if they have a uniform violation, and when asked about it leading up to the Seattle game, Bears coach <b>Ben Johnson</b> said he was confident Williams wouldn’t do anything that would hurt the team.</p><p>Caddix has seized on the marketing momentum of Williams putting their cleats in the spotlight and bought billboard space in Chicago advertising that it is paying his fines. When a video surfaced of Williams wearing his unmarked cleats in pre-game warmups, the company’s X account posted, “No logo necessary!”</p><p>Caddix says roughly 60 players are wearing its cleats this season, and Williams has been adamant about sticking with them because he believes in their claim that they reduce non-contact knee and ankle injuries.</p><p>He wore an all-white version of the cleats in the preseason and in his first two games, including when he hurt his hamstring, and the company’s logo didn’t stand out enough to bother the NFL.</p><p>Williams does not have an endorsement deal with Caddix or any other brand in order to maintain freedom to wear whatever he pleases. He also has worn Nike and New Balance shoes in his career.</p><h3><b>Bagent on block?</b></h3><h3></h3><p>The Bears are unlikely to make any more splashy trades after acquiring defensive tackle <b>Jeffery Simmons</b> — <b>Khalil Mack</b> is still a possibility — but there’s a good chance they’ll get called about backup quarterback <b>Tyson Bagent</b>.</p><p>The Ravens lost starter <b>Lamar Jackson</b>, possibly for the season, and backup <b>Tyler Huntley</b> this week and probably don’t want to concede their season at 4-4 in the wide-open AFC North. Plus, former Bears assistant <b>Declan Doyle</b> is their offensive coordinator.</p><h3><b>Simmons tribute</b></h3><h3></h3><p> Simmons started for the Bears in his debut, but his old team hasn’t forgotten him. Several Titans defenders wore red arm sleeves Sunday against the Bengals in their first game without him — a nod to Simmons’ trademark.</p><p>“We just wanted to let Jeff know we’re thinking of him and we love him,” defensive end <b>Solomon Thomas</b> said. “He was an unbelievable leader... I've never seen a player of his caliber work the way he works.</p><p>"When someone like that leaves your room, you can’t just move on from it. We wanted to show him how much he means to us.”</p><h3><b>Muhammad out</b></h3><h3></h3><p>Bears rookie cornerback <b>Malik Muhammad</b>, who has developed into a starter, was out with toe injury. It was his first missed game.</p>
entries.author: Jason Lieser

entries.title: Veteran big man Nic Claxton moves closer to making his Bulls debut
entries.summary: <p>PHILADELPHIA – Help is on the way … finally.</p><p>And the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bulls" >Bulls</a> could use it. Then again, who couldn’t use a 6-foot-11 athletic big who protects the basket and is an elite rim runner?</p><p>Coach <b>Tiago Splitter</b> said Monday that offseason acquisition <b>Nic Claxton</b> went through a full practice Sunday — his first since he injured his hamstring just before the start of training camp.</p><p>“He’s working with the team,” Splitter said. “We had a good practice — not long, but short and intense, and he was able to be in the entire practice with the guys, and that’s a good sign. He’s progressing with the plan, and we’ll figure out the best game for him to come back.”</p><p>The Bulls face the Knicks on Wednesday in New York, then have a three-game homestand against the 76ers, Spurs and Hawks. Splitter was leaning toward a return sometime in that span as long as there are no setbacks.</p><p>“It could be, yeah,” he said.</p><p>What will Claxton add? Initially, he’s likely to play on restricted minutes and come off the bench. But if the Bulls get the apex version of Claxton from his days as a starting center for the Nets, they’ll instantly have a much better defense just from a rim-protection standpoint. Claxton averaged 2.5 blocks per game in the 2022-23 season in Brooklyn and 2.1 the next season.</p><p>He’ll also give the Bulls another long athlete in transition, creating another lob-threat option for guards such as <b>Josh Giddey</b> and <b>Tre Jones</b>.</p><p>The only unknown is who would be bumped out of the rotation. Splitter has been using a second unit of <b>Zach Collins</b>, <b>Isaac Okoro</b>, Jones, <b>Noa Essengue</b> and <b>Leonard Miller</b>. If Claxton is used as a starter, <b>Jalen Smith</b> drops down to a second-unit spot, and Splitter already has said he leans on a 10-man rotation at most. That means Miller and Essengue likely would compete to keep the final spot.</p><p><b>Speaking of . . .</b></p><p>As the Bulls continue to help Essengue find a path to keeping a rotation role, his job for now is simple: Play defense and more defense and worry about the other stuff later. He’s being put on opposing perimeter players and picking up some guards full-court.</p><p>“He can slide in front of people, he’s long, [and] he and Isaac are the best on our team at doing that,” Splitter said. “He can pick up guys at full-court. Just his ability to move his feet — it’s elite, to be honest.</p><p>“He still makes mistakes. He’s a 19-year-old kid that is learning to compete at the highest level. [But] I think he can be a tremendous defensive player one day in<br>this league.”</p><p><b>The kids can take it</b></p><p>There’s a reason individual Bulls players haven’t had many days off. Splitter and his coaching staff believe there’s simply too much work to do — too many pieces of his installation they’re still working to learn.</p><p>It helps that this team is made up of mostly young players who don’t need days off in the early part of the season like older players might.</p><p>“I think it’s a young team, [and] they have the legs to do that,” Splitter said. “A vet is different, a vet team. We’ve got to work, we’ve got to get better, and I’d rather have them a little bit sore in a game than not putting in the work.”</p>
entries.author: Joe Cowley

entries.title: First day of practice: Marmion goes co-ed, jumps straight into the fire with a varsity girls basketball team
entries.summary: <p>After averaging more than 20 wins across 25 seasons in stops at IC Catholic, Lisle and Marian Catholic, Dan Murray stepped away from coaching girls basketball last year.</p><p>But it was a pause rather than a hard stop. Murray joined the faculty at Marmion and laid the foundation for the first girls team in the school's 93-year history.</p><p>Marmion has gone co-ed, admitting around 40 freshmen and sophomore girls this school year. The 11 who are on the girls basketball team got to work Monday as practice opened around the state.</p><p>"I'll be honest with you," Murray told the Sun-Times during a break in practice. "It was very difficult last year, not coaching and not being in it after so long. And obviously it's something I love to do. It really lets you know how much it means to you."</p><p>Marmion is adding a few other girls sports this school year and will start more next year as more girls enroll. Most will start at the junior-varsity level, but Murray and his players are jumping right into the fire. They'll play a varsity schedule and will be in Class 3A for the IHSA playoffs.</p><p>"We did want kids to know that we were taking this very seriously in terms of wanting to build a strong program," Murray said. "Hopefully kids who really love the game of basketball and aspire to do some things at the high school level and possibly beyond would take a look at us."</p><div class="Enhancement" entries.title: Blackhawks debut new green Hometown Remix jerseys to tepid fan reaction
entries.summary: <p>The Blackhawks debuted their new green jerseys — a not-so-well-kept secret for the last several weeks — on Monday against the Avalanche.</p><p>They’re quite similar to the jerseys the Hawks used to wear for St. Patrick’s Day before the NHL banned specialty warmup jerseys in 2023. The color theme is built out from the green second feather in the primary logo, and the shoulders are adorned with the alternate ‘‘crossed C’’ logo.</p><p>Those green St. Patrick’s jerseys long have been popular, and you typically will see a few fans donning them at the United Center at any given game. In the past, not many NHL teams had been able to pull off a color outside their usual scheme so well.</p><p>But that changed Monday with the official release of the Hometown Remix, Fanatics’ new set of alternate jerseys for all 32 teams.</p><p>There are some striking looks in the collection. The Panthers nailed their pink ‘‘Miami Vice’’ sweater, as did the Ducks with their green, purple and yellow ‘‘Mighty Ducks’’ sweater. The Kings now have a new purple throwback jersey, the Bruins now have a brown jersey and a bunch of teams now have black jerseys with vivid accents.</p><p>The originality and creativity of many of those jerseys likely contributed to a lackluster fan reaction toward the Hawks’ new green sweaters, considering those already have been done before in almost identical form. They’re also quite similar to the Stars’ regular home jerseys, which many people pointed out.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">Here are the official photos of the Blackhawks’ new green Hometown Remix jersey, which they’ll debut tonight against the Avalanche.<br><br>Also wearing them 12/29 vs Vegas and four times in March.<br><br>Thoughts? <a href="https://t.co/lM3VjLy2zu">pic.twitter.com/lM3VjLy2zu</a></p>— Ben Pope (@BenPopeCST) <a href="https://x.com/BenPopeCST/status/2117271752397205563?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">November 2, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>It’s worth noting there are a few differences from the old St. Patrick’s jerseys. The secondary color is tan, not white, and the collar is now black (with tan laces below it). Four stars — like those in the Chicago flag — are embossed into the sleeve stripes. I personally liked the brownish-tan gloves the Hawks wore Monday.</p><p>But Hawks fans have been inundated with jersey releases lately, considering the team wore special red centennial jerseys last season and debuted new black jerseys — a nostalgic throwback to the 1990s — last November that remain in the rotation this season.</p><p>And given the Hawks’ on-ice struggles, it simply might be impossible for the fan base to get too excited about anything right now.</p><p>The Hawks will wear these new green jerseys again Dec. 29 against the Golden Knights, plus four times between March 8 and March 16 leading up to St. Patrick’s Day. They typically wear their black alternate jerseys on Fridays.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" data-embed> <iframe width="113" height="200" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/N6StHPgRXdc?feature=oembed" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen title="Blackhawks debut their new green uniforms"></iframe> </div> </div></div><p><b>Internal data</b></p><p>Hawks coach Jeff Blashill's morning news conference Monday contained a couple interesting tidbits.</p><p>The first pertained to the team's games last week against the Kings and Bruins, which Blashill said were "two of the top five games we've had in the last four years" based on a stat they track internally called "on-puck action...which basically measures execution offensively."</p><p>The Hawks haven't played many great games over the last four years, which sets a low bar. And they did play very well in those two games last week, despite losing to the Bruins. In between, their "on-puck action" in the Red Wings game was surely much worse.</p><p><b>Three centers</b></p><p>The second interesting tidbit pertained to Connor Bedard, Frank Nazar and Anton Frondell all playing center, with Blashill squashing any hopes of Frondell moving up to Bedard's wing anytime soon.</p><p>"[I'm] not in a hurry to move any of those guys out of their natural positions," he said. "Ultimately, you have to have three dangerous lines...or at least three lines with big roles in this league to be a really good team."</p>

entries.title: Quincy man accused of mailing suspicious letters to elected officials to remain in custody
entries.summary: <p>A Quincy man accused of sending suspicious letters to members of Congress will remain in custody while awaiting trial after waiving his right to fight prosecutors' bid to keep him detained.</p><p>Matthew Unglesbee, 36, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/2026/10/26/quincy-man-charged-mailed-letters-white-powder-congress-members-unglesbee" target="_blank" ><u>faces charges</u></a> of mailing threatening communications, false information and hoaxes, according to the complaint filed in the Central District of Illinois. A jury trial is set to begin Dec. 7.</p><p>Unglesbee told a judge he understood the decision and had not been threatened or offered anything in exchange for the decision.</p><p>“We will concede to detention,” federal public defender Roxanne Mendez Johnson said at a hearing Monday. Johnson has been appointed to represent Unglesbee.</p><p>The charges follow several <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/2026/10/16/schneider-quigleys-offices-receive-suspicious-letters-amid-pre-election-threats" target="_blank" ><u>Illinois lawmakers reporting receiving suspicious mail</u></a> in recent weeks, including Democratic U.S. Reps. Mike Quigley, Brad Schneider and Jan Schakowsky.</p><p>Sen. Tammy Duckworth’s Chicago office also confirmed receiving two suspicious letters in recent weeks.</p><p>During an interview with law enforcement, Unglesbee allegedly admitted in writing that he sent letters containing a white, granular substance and handwritten messages, including “HA HA” and “HAH enjoy the gift,” according to an FBI affidavit. Preliminary testing found no toxins in the substance.</p><p>During an interview with FBI agents, Unglesbee allegedly said the substance was salt and that he used it because it resembled anthrax, according to the affidavit. Unglesbee claimed he was joking but also said he knew the powder would be taken seriously and would have “hazmat come in white suits.”</p><p>The letters were postmarked in Springfield on Oct. 19. While searching Unglesbee’s home, investigators also found an empty, unmailed envelope addressed to a congressional office in Washington, D.C.</p><p>The complaint against Unglesbee does not identify the four congressional recipients by name, though Quigley and Schakowsky, whose offices each received a second round of letters, issued separate statements indicating the arrest was in connection with the letters their offices had received.</p>

entries.title: Bears race to 5-2 start, but winning NFC North remains crucial to Super Bowl hopes
entries.summary: <p>SEATTLE — The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> have been talking Super Bowl ever since the end of last season, and things got a bit louder when <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/31/jeffery-simmons-trade-bears-gm-ryan-poles-pursues-legendary-stuff-as-super-bowl-chase-officially-begins" target="_blank" >they traded for star defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons</a> last week.</p><p>Before they get to all that, however, it’s going to be brutal surviving the NFC North.</p><p>As good as the Bears felt about standing 5-2 going into their game Monday at the defending champion Seahawks — and rightfully so — that left them in third place in their own division and just inside the cut for the playoffs.</p><p>The Bears, of course, don’t think they’re the third-best team in the division, and neither do the oddsmakers. Before their game against the Seahawks, the Bears had the sixth-best odds to win the Super Bowl at 12-1, with the Vikings 10th, the Lions 13th and the Packers 15th.</p><p>Sportsbooks don’t decide the standings, but that’s a reasonable outlook on the future of the division rather than going off how it stands at the moment.</p><p>The other relatively safe forecast at this point is that it’s going to be an absolute battle in the last two months of the regular season.</p><p>The NFC North was the only division in the NFL last season to have every team finish with a winning record, and it’s tracking toward repeating that feat. The four teams were a combined 16-3 in non-division games entering Monday.</p><p>There are no freebies in the division, and the Bears already lost what would figure to be their most favorable matchup, falling 9-3 to the Vikings at Soldier Field when quarterback Caleb Williams went down in Week 2. The Vikings are 6-1. And while the consensus is they won’t be able to sustain that level, they have the No. 2 defense in the league and had a lead against the Lions with five minutes left Sunday at Ford Field before taking their first loss.</p><p>The Bears are in a hole at 0-2 in the division — the other loss was a blowout defeat to the Packers at Lambeau Field with Tyson Bagent at quarterback — and will have to make up ground down the stretch. They visit the Lions on Thanksgiving, then close the season hosting the Packers and Lions in Weeks 16 and 17 before visiting the Vikings in Week 18.</p><p>The Bears managed to win the division last season despite going 2-4 in it, but they were the first team to do that since 2010, and the odds of pulling it off again are slim.</p><p>There will be minimal margin for error for the Bears, given what a favorable draw the NFC North got in the scheduling model this season. Every team in the division is playing the NFC South (they’re 7-2 against that group so far) and AFC East (5-1).</p><p>The teams also each will face a squad from the AFC South, where the Jaguars are the only club in the division that isn’t a disaster. The Bears will host them in Week 13, whereas everyone else in the NFC North will play a team that’s 2-5 or worse right now.</p><p>It’s only going to get tougher, too, with the Packers expecting to get star linebacker Micah Parsons back from a knee injury soon and the Lions and Vikings weighing whether to make big moves before the trade deadline next Tuesday.</p><p>Winning the division is crucial to the Bears’ championship hopes because it would change their playoff path completely. After taking the NFC North last season, they had two home playoff games. Had they and the 49ers reached the NFC Championship Game instead of the Rams and Seahawks, that would have been at Soldier Field, too.</p><p>The visit Monday to thunderous Lumen Field emphasized how important playing at home would be. Opponents don’t want to come here any more often than they have to.</p><p>The first question the Bears must answer is whether they’re truly better than the other three teams in their division.</p><p>• They can claim that with the Packers on the grounds of beating them twice in three games last season, including in the playoffs, and put a justifiable asterisk on the loss last month at Lambeau Field because they didn’t have Williams.</p><p>• They can’t make a peep when it comes to the Lions, who destroyed them early last season and clamped down on their offense at the end of it.</p><p>• They can shake off the early loss to the Vikings as an anomaly, but they can’t dismiss how well defensive coordinator extraordinaire Brian Flores outmaneuvered Williams and coach Ben Johnson that day. He’s good enough to do it again.</p><p>The Bears will get a chance to make definitive statements on all three fronts at the end of the season. It’s a near-certainty the division will be tight going into those last three weeks, and the Bears probably will need a sweep of those games to come out on top.</p>
entries.author: Jason Lieser

entries.title: Michael Wilbon, longtime ESPN commentator, is taking a leave of absence for 'health issues'
entries.summary: <p>Michael Wilbon is taking a break.</p><p>The longtime ESPN commentator and co-host of the network's popular "Pardon the Interruption" talk show alongside good friend Tony Kornheiser announced Monday he is taking a leave of absence because of what he described as "multiple health issues."</p><p>Wilbon, a Chicago native who turns 68 later this month, wrote in a post on X that he is taking a trip to "the injured list" but added he hopes it is "not an extended one."</p><p>While Wilbon, who is also featured on ESPN's NBA coverage, declined to go into full detail about what he is facing, he said during his weekly appearance on Kornheiser's podcast on Monday that he is diabetic and that is "part of what I'm dealing with now, but not the entirety of it."</p><p>Wilbon's last appearance on "PTI," which recently celebrated its 25th anniversary and is credited with revolutionizing television's "sports debate" format, was on Oct. 26.</p><p>"I didn't do the show for a week because I was just exhausted," Wilbon told Kornheiser. "Beyond exhausted, lifeless. And this has been going on for a while."</p><p>Wilbon, a Northwestern alum and member of the school's board of trustees, stressed that his decision is not a retirement and he plans to return at some point, adding that his symptoms became too significant to ignore.</p><p>"I have to listen," he said to Kornheiser. "I've got things going on that are forcing me to listen."</p><p>The show, in part, is a byproduct of the friendship of Wilbon and Kornheiser, who became colleagues at the Washington Post in the 1980s.</p><p>"I have loved sparring and hosting PTI with Tony every single day these past 25 years," Wilbon wrote. "And I'm incredibly grateful for the support and encouragement of my colleagues as I take this time away to concentrate on me, especially my well-being."<br></p>
entries.author: AP

entries.title: White Sox skipper Will Venable named a finalist for AL Manager of the Year
entries.summary: <p>In winning 84 games during the regular season, earning the franchise’s first playoff berth in five years and coming one win shy of playing for the American League pennant, the 2026 <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox" >White Sox</a> were a lot better than anyone expected.</p><p>That has a way of leading to hardware for leadership, and on cue, the White Sox’ second-year skipper Will Venable has been named a finalist for AL Manager of the Year. Chad Tracy of the Red Sox, who took over midseason for a club that rallied for wild card berth, and Kevin Cash, the longtime manager of the AL champion Rays, are the other two finalists.</p><p>In his first year on the job, Venable oversaw a 19-win improvement from a 2024 White Sox team that suffered through the losingest season in MLB history. In his second year, Venable seemingly one-upped himself by guiding his club to a 24-win increase and a playoff run that both surprised and electrified the league. Players raved about the unique level of team chemistry that flourished under Venable from the outset of spring training, and continued doing so through postgame media access of their Game 5 loss in the ALDS.</p><p>Addressing reporters after the season, Sox general manager Chris Getz said he expected Venable’s complete coaching staff to return in light of the team’s success, and has expressed interest in ensuring the skipper remains a long-term dugout fixture on the South Side.</p><p>“We've got a really special manager in Will Venable that recognizes the power of the clubhouse,” Getz said last month. “We had so many young players that came up to the big leagues and performed. It wasn't perfect. It didn't need to be perfect and because of that approach, thought process and patience, it kept the group motivated and hungry. Even through their struggles, they were still finding ways to win baseball games.”</p><p>Venable will potentially be the sixth White Sox manager to win the award in franchise history, and the first since Ozzie Guillen in the World Series-winning year of 2005. Jerry Manuel, Jeff Torborg, Tony La Russa and Chuck Tanner are the other past Sox winners.</p>
entries.author: James Fegan
